source.title: Schedule Trigger runs daily workflows twice on DST fall-back night (Europe/Berlin)

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

On 25 Oct 2026 the clocks in Germany went back (03:00 CEST to 02:00 CET). Every daily Schedule Trigger I have at 03:xx ran twice, one hour apart:
- Days interval at 03:00: 01:00:58Z and 02:00:58Z
- Days interval at 03:45: 01:45:57Z and 02:45:57Z
- cron `0 15 3 * * *`: 01:15:00Z and 02:15:00Z

The first run falls in the repeated hour (the second 02:xx), the second one is the real 03:xx. All 8 of my daily triggers at 03:xx did this, in interval and in cron mode. A daily trigger at 02:45 ran once, and the triggers at 04:xx and the hourly ones ran normally. Both runs have mode trigger and the same seconds offset.

I run the legacy scheduler (N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED not set), which uses cron 4.4.0 with luxon 3.7.2. My image is the official one plus a few patched OS and npm packages (not cron or luxon). This looks like the same bug as:
- https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron/issues/1087 (see the comment from 4 Oct about daily jobs in the hour after the repeated hour)
- https://github.com/nestjs/schedule/issues/2389 (same double run, same date and timezone, cron 4.4.0)
cron 4.4.0 is still the latest stable release, so there's no fixed version to upgrade to yet. The comment on kelektiv/node-cron#1087 also shows this for America/New_York with daily jobs at 02:xx. US clocks go back on 1 Nov 2026.

Workaround: I moved the jobs where a second run hurts to 04:xx.

### To Reproduce

1. Self-hosted n8n with GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Europe/Berlin and TZ=Europe/Berlin, N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED not set.
2. Activate a workflow with a Schedule Trigger that runs daily at 03:00.
3. Let it run through a DST fall-back night (or fake the clock).
4. On 25 Oct 2026 it ran at 01:00Z and again at 02:00Z.

### Expected behavior

One run per day, at 03:00 local time (02:00Z on 25 Oct).
